yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point is kept, with added asides: "(more than once! the old goat)", "empty as a pub at sunrise", "read and read and read till the cows come home". These hang off the original, though "Fair dinkum." and "Stuck fast." are padding.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms mostly fit: "noggin", "chockers", "a ripper of a time". "downed tools on our former works in parallelopipeds" strains a little in the mock-formal report, but carries "abandoned".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Some lines are natural ("I haven't let on to anybody, mind", "what she's on about"), but stock phrases are bolted on: "Fair dinkum.", "till the cows come home", "empty as a pub at sunrise", "a dead important one".
yarn-troppo.register: The brief is level 2, but the slang is heavy: "noggin", "salt-and-pepper job", "Fair dinkum.", "ripper", "chockers", "Hooroo", "Chrissie", "the old goat". Closer to level 3-4. No swearing, as asked.
yarn-troppo.tone: Judy's chirpy, teasing voice mostly survives ("Oh, you see, I know!"), but the pub-flavoured additions ("empty as a pub at sunrise", "the old goat") roughen a schoolgirl's letter.
yarn-troppo.flow: Readable, with pile-ups: "a sort of sprinkly grey, salt-and-pepper job, or maybe nothing up there at all" and "Stuck fast." after "I _am_ stuck".
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range of slang with little repetition: "noggin", "chockers", "ripper", "Hooroo", "See ya", "on the go", "snuck off".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the letter, its question and its reading list, but the additions push it towards a yarn: "the old goat", "Fair dinkum."

engine.meaning: Essentially the original word for word, so everything survives: "You never answered my question and it was very important."
engine.sense: The few swaps mostly fit ("verandah roof", "heaps of others"), but "I’m going to have a beautiful time in holiday" renders "in vacation" ungrammatically.
engine.authenticity: What little Aussie there is ("beaut red bath robe", "merry Chrissie!") sits next to untouched US forms: "Good-by, Daddy", "Good-by till January--and a merry Chrissie!", "a beautiful time in holiday".
engine.register: Largely untranslated: apart from spelling ("colour", "realising") and "verandah", "heaps", "beaut", "Chrissie", it is the original. Lighter than level 2.
engine.tone: The original's voice is intact because the text is: "Oh, you see, I know! You’re a snappy old thing with a temper."
engine.flow: Reads as the original, except the broken join "a beautiful time in holiday" and the mismatched "Good-by till January--and a merry Chrissie!"
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, since it barely changes: "ARE YOU BALD?"

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Everything is there, closely tracked: "I've got you worked out exactly--very satisfactorily, too--", "bought it with $1.12 of last month's allowance".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Each term fits: "four on the go at once", "what she's on about", "Hooroo, Daddy", "a beaut time over the holidays".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, unforced Australian: "If you can't be bothered writing", "The corridors are that cluttered", "cos there are eighteen blank years behind me". "my beaut red bath robe" is slightly odd.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, steady touch, right for level 2: "cos", "beaut", "Turns out", "Hooroo", "See ya in January--and a merry Chrissie!". No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Judy's bright, teasing voice comes through: "Oh, you see, I know! You're a snappy old thing with a temper on you." The mock-formal Saturday report stays mock-formal.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "I've got a new rule, and it's unbreakable: never, ever study at night".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied, though "beaut" appears twice ("beaut red bath robe", "a beaut time").
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the letter, retold lightly: "But here's the problem: shall I add some hair?"

unharnessed.meaning: All points survive: "there's another Freshman from Texas staying back too", "(that _would_ mark me as a bit odd)". "and pretty well, too" softens "very satisfactorily" slightly.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "chock-a-block", "staying back", "dressing-gown", "crabby old thing". "left by the wayside" for "getting left out" is a fair fit.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Australian English: "hop into my nice red dressing-gown", "The corridors are so chock-a-block", "Hooroo, Daddy". Nothing stagey.
unharnessed.register: Light, maybe a shade lighter than level 2: "chock-a-block", "Hooroo", "on the go", but it ends "Bye till January--and a merry Christmas!"
unharnessed.tone: The voice is kept: "Oh, you see, I know! You're a crabby old thing with a temper on you." "crabby" loses a little of the fond "snappy".
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth, but "a sort of sprinkly grey sort of hair" repeats "sort of", and "I've got it all worked out exactly what you look like" is a clumsy join.
unharnessed.variety: Varied but sparse: "chock-a-block", "staying back", "Hooroo", "on the go", "on about".
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the original, its question and reading list: "Here's your portrait:"

dinkum-3.meaning: Mostly complete, but some details are flattened: "very satisfactorily" is dropped ("I've got you all worked out--down to a tee--"), "a properly assorted family" becomes "a proper family", and "studying is getting left out" becomes "nobody's doing any study".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit well: "last month's pocket money" for allowance, "first-year" for Freshman, "chockers", "let on". "at uni" for college fits Australian usage.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural: "I haven't let on to anybody", "The stuff most girls ... just soak up", "If you can't be bothered writing".
dinkum-3.register: Right weight for level 2: "cos", "chockers", "beaut", "Hooroo", "See ya", "Chrissie", with no swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Judy's voice is warm and teasing: "You're a cranky old thing with a temper, I reckon."
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "I've got a new rule, and there's no breaking it: never, ever study at night".
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "down to a tee", "mates", "chockers", "pocket money", "first-year", "uni", "Hooroo", "See ya".
dinkum-3.essence: Recognisably the letter, with a little flattening of its period wit: "a proper family" for "a properly assorted family".

yarn-troppo.why: Stock Aussie tag bolted onto the end of a paragraph; nothing in the original calls for it.

yarn-troppo.quote: the whole lot of them empty as a pub at sunrise
yarn-troppo.original: because there are eighteen blank years behind me
yarn-troppo.why: Forced simile, and a pub image is out of character for a college girl at level 2.

yarn-troppo.original: I didn’t know that Henry the Eighth was married more than once
yarn-troppo.why: Added aside; colour, but heavier than the brief.

yarn-troppo.quote: a sort of sprinkly grey, salt-and-pepper job
read and read and read till the cows come home
yarn-troppo.why: Stock idiom bolted on to a repetition that already did the work.

engine.quote: I’m going to have a beautiful time in holiday
engine.original: I’m going to have a beautiful time in vacation
engine.why: Mechanical swap leaves broken grammar; an Australian says 'over the holidays'.

engine.quote: Good-by till January--and a merry Chrissie!
engine.original: Good-by till January--and a merry Christmas!
engine.why: Archaic US 'Good-by' left beside a slang 'Chrissie'; the mix jars.

engine.quote: You never answered my question and it was very important.
engine.original: You never answered my question and it was very important.
engine.why: The text is largely left untranslated, well under the level-2 brief.

yarn-dinkum.why: 'Beaut' as attributive for a bathrobe is a touch forced, and it is repeated later in 'a beaut time'.

unharnessed.quote: a sort of sprinkly grey sort of hair
I've got it all worked out exactly what you look like
unharnessed.original: I have it planned exactly what you look like

dinkum-3.quote: The stuff most girls with a proper family and a home and mates and a library just soak up
dinkum-3.original: most girls with a properly assorted family and a home and friends and a library know by absorption
dinkum-3.why: Loses the comic 'properly assorted' that marks the orphan's view.

dinkum-3.quote: everyone's so excited that nobody's doing any study
dinkum-3.original: everybody is so bubbling over with excitement that studying is getting left out

dinkum-3.quote: I've got you all worked out--down to a tee--right up to the top of your head
dinkum-3.original: I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily--until I reach the top of your head

summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and full of meaning, but overdone for a level-2 brief, with stock phrases bolted on.
summaries.engine: Faithful because barely touched; a few swaps, one of them ungrammatical.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Light, natural and faithful; exactly the weight of a level-2 brief.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural and faithful, slightly light on Aussie, with a couple of clumsy joins.
summaries.dinkum-3: Natural, varied and on-brief, with a few small flattenings.
